newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1-private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $1-private.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by ample hog runs and pork output which has pressured pork prices recently, livestock dealers said and packer buyers said.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants could range from $54.50 to $55.50, sources there said.
Illinois hogs at plants could sell from $54.00 to $54.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices may also be $54.00 to $54.50.
Expanded slaughter produced more than adequate supplies of pork, which weighed on wholesale prices, several sources noted.

Slaughter Wednesday was pegged at 368,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 1.068 million head, USDA said. The weekly number was up 1.2 percent from a week ago and up 2.4 percent from a year ago.
At midday, loins were quoted down mostly $4.00 per cwt, butts were down $2.00 to $4.00, heavy hams were mostly $3.00 lower and pork bellies were down $1.00 to $2.00, USDA said.
However, the lower prices did move some pork, market sources said. USDA reported that 85.4 loads of fabricated cuts and 13.5 loads of trimmings had sold as of midday Wednesday.
